svg.title: Structure of an optically thin radiative shock
svg.desc: Top: the gas flows from left to right. Region 1 is cold gas moving rapidly, with rho_1, p_1, T_1 and u_1. A double line, the viscous shock, separates it from region 2, hot gas moving slowly, with rho_2, p_2, T_2 and u_2. The gas then cools in a radiative relaxation layer, which ends in region 3, cold gas moving very slowly, with rho_3, p_3, T_3 and u_3. Below, two profiles aligned with the regions: the density jumps from rho_1 to rho_2 at the shock and then keeps increasing to rho_3 in the relaxation layer; the temperature jumps from T_1 to T_2 at the shock and then decreases to T_3, close to T_1.

g.font-family: 'Latin Modern Math', 'STIX Two Math', 'Cambria Math', serif
